problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(s)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(s-2)\,i+(1-s)\,j+{s}^{2}\,k.$
worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\operatorname{ln}⁡(s-2)$ is $s\in (2,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $1-s$ is $s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component ${s}^{2}$ is $s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14033854/assets/91b196d5e312c4242a493f65abad556aa7f689640b09e0c51bc9124681abb48a.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(s)$ is $s\in (2,\infty ).$
